## The task

Take the EVM reporter from Lab 9 and deliberately feed it the seeded-anomaly dataset from Week 9's studio.

**Deliverable.** What it reported, whether it caught the anomaly, and a one-page governance note: what control would have caught this before the report reached a sponsor? This is the core question of your final project's AI section.

## Tutor prompt for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after.

```text
Be my tutor on stakeholders, sponsorship, and organizational structure. One
question at a time. Test me hard on the evidence about top management
support — including its methodological weaknesses. Make me design a study
that would break the endogeneity problem.
```

## The weekly loop

This lab is step 4–6 of the loop. The whole cycle:

```text
1. TUTOR (diagnostic)  — 10 min — what do I already wrongly believe?
2. Read the module     — 20 min — notes + one primary source
3. TUTOR (voice)       — 20 min — one question at a time, no lecturing
4. Write something     — 15 min — a plan, an argument, a worked problem
5. EDITOR              — 10 min — attack what I wrote
6. ROOMMATE            —  5 min — where else does this structure appear?
7. TUTOR (retrieval)   —  5 min — mixed questions from all prior weeks
```

Steps 4 and 5 do the work. A loop that stops after step 3 feels productive and mostly isn't.
